rules:
Work only inside this workspace.
The file named in the task is your answer. Edit it in place.
You may write and run your own tests with Icarus Verilog.
Do not use the network or web search.
Do not look for tests, reference solutions or grading files. None are provided.
instructions:
## Knowledge base

A knowledge base built from earlier debugging tasks is available at `/kb`. An agent like you wrote it. Nothing in it has been verified: its author never learned whether a fix passed. Treat it as a colleague's notes and trust your own tests over it. It may be empty.

Look at it before you start work on the task, using the conventions below.

**Entries are notes.** A note is a markdown file holding one lesson, in whatever form suits it. Say what you tried that did not work as well as what did, when the note applies, and which task it came from (the module and the kind of bug). Add a note only when a task taught you something worth keeping, and revise an existing note in preference to adding a near-duplicate.

**Entries are separate files** under `/kb/entries`, named by a number and a short title, with no index. List the folder and search it by text to find what bears on your task. When you add an entry, give it the next number.
update_prompt:
The task is finished. Now update the knowledge base at `/kb` so that it is more useful for the next task, which will be a different design with a different bug.

You were not told whether your fix is correct, so record what you observed and did, not that it worked. Follow the conventions you were given for what an entry is and how entries are arranged, and keep any index consistent with the entries. If the task taught you nothing worth keeping and the conventions do not require an entry, change nothing.
